channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan launches 72 industrial and 91 social projects ahead of Independence Day
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched 72 industrial and service projects and 91 social facilities worth nearly 50 trillion soums. These projects are expected to create 15,000 jobs and generate an additional 1 trillion soums in annual budget revenue. The economy has grown 2.5 times in ten years, attracting $160 billion in foreign investment and launching 2,163 major industrial projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan ready to strengthen comprehensive strategic partnership with China, says President Tokayev
item.description: Kazakhstan is prepared to consistently strengthen its eternal comprehensive strategic partnership with China, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated in an interview. He noted the high level of current relations, emphasizing shared borders and a long history of good neighborliness. The partnership encompasses trade, investment, energy, transport, industry, agriculture, digitalization, and culture.

item.title: Uzbekistan Delegation Attends Belgrade Summit on Non-Aligned Movement's 65th Anniversary
item.description: Uzbekistan's delegation, led by Sodik Safoev, participated in a high-level meeting in Belgrade commemorating the 65th anniversary of the Non-Aligned Movement. Safoev discussed the movement's current significance and Uzbekistan's preparation to chair it from 2027-2030, highlighting priorities like peace, security, economy, climate change, and youth issues.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Exports to Hong Kong Surge 22-Fold to $716 Million
item.description: Uzbekistan's exports to Hong Kong reached nearly $716 million in January-July, a 22-fold increase from $32.5 million in the same period last year, according to the National Statistics Committee. This growth propelled Hong Kong to become Uzbekistan's sixth-largest export market, surpassing Turkey and Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: New Book Explores Uzbekistan's Transformation Through the Lens of its Women
item.description: A new book by Egyptian scholars Dr. Nabila Kandil and Dr. Ahmed Al-Zubaidi examines Uzbekistan's transformation and the role of women in its societal and national development. Published by Dar Al-Mustakbal Al-Arabi, the work analyzes the country's progress under the 'New Uzbekistan' concept.

item.title: New Head Appointed for Uzbekistan's Migration Agency
item.description: Muxsinxo‘ja Abdurahmonov has been appointed the new director of the Migration Agency under the Cabinet of Ministers of Uzbekistan. He previously served as Uzbekistan's Ambassador to Japan since July 2021. Abdurahmonov replaces Behzod Musayev, who was dismissed to take up other duties.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Ambassador to Japan Appointed Head of Migration Agency
item.description: Behzod Musayev has been dismissed as director of the Migration Agency. Muxsinxo‘ja Abdurahmonov, who previously served as Uzbekistan's Ambassador to Japan, has been appointed as the new head of the agency. The decision was signed by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Tourism Head Predicts 30 Million Tourists Post-SCO Summit
item.description: Following the SCO and World Nomad Games, Kyrgyzstan expects a significant tourism surge, potentially reaching 20-30 million visitors annually. Eduard Kubatov, head of the State Agency for Tourism, stated that global media coverage has increased interest in the country. He urged citizens to prepare for hosting tourists.

item.title: Uzbekistan to transform poverty reduction and income growth system
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev chaired a meeting on enhancing poverty reduction and income growth strategies. The poverty rate has decreased from 5.8% to 3.9%, with 1.5 million people now needing assistance. Despite significant resource allocation, regional effectiveness in poverty reduction varies.

item.title: Uzbek President's Administration Head Meets with Emir of Qatar in Doha
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, Head of the Administration of the President of Uzbekistan, met with the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, in Doha. They discussed strengthening bilateral relations and exploring new joint initiatives, noting significant potential for cooperation.

item.title: Iran considers Uzbekistan an important partner in Central Asia, says ambassador
item.description: Iran views Uzbekistan as a key partner in Central Asia, according to Iranian Ambassador Mukhammadali Iskandariy. He highlighted Uzbekistan's growing regional importance, driven by its economic, historical, and civilizational potential, and its foreign policy focused on good neighborliness and constructive dialogue.

item.title: Deputy suggests officials hindering democracy lack constitutional knowledge
item.description: Deputy Bobur Bekmurodov proposed that officials hindering democracy often lack sufficient knowledge of the Constitution. He suggested that state employees should be tested on their understanding of the Constitution.

item.title: German official praises Uzbekistan's reforms and future prospects
item.description: Johann Saathoff, Parliamentary State Secretary for Economic Cooperation and Development, stated that Uzbekistan's reforms in vocational education, public administration, and employment are creating a solid foundation for a bright future. He noted that these processes enhance the country's international authority and foster cooperation within Central Asia.

item.title: 1.2 km of Bus Rapid Transit lane opened on Shahrisabz Street in Tashkent.
item.description: A 1.2 km section of a Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) lane has been opened on Shahrisabz Street in Tashkent. The first phase of the project covers the area from the roundabout connecting Shahrisabz, Mirobod, and Shota Rustaveli streets to the intersection with Amir Temur Avenue.

item.title: Violations found in Kayyndy River water protection zone in Kyrgyzstan's Talas region.
item.description: Violations of land and water legislation were discovered in the village of Kayyndy, Talas region, Kyrgyzstan. The Ministry of Agriculture reported that light structures were built in the river's water protection zone, some close to the water. Soil cover was also damaged.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan plans to build a factory for producing vaccines against viruses and foot-and-mouth disease
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to construct a factory for producing biological preparations, including vaccines against viral and bacterial diseases, and foot-and-mouth disease. The project aims to strengthen the country's veterinary security and establish domestic vaccine production. Construction of veterinary laboratories is also being discussed.

item.title: Uzbek President discusses strengthening strategic partnership with US Senator
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held discussions with a US Senator regarding further strengthening the strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and the United States. The parties also reviewed the development of inter-parliamentary cooperation.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva meets with the Emir of Qatar to discuss expanding relations.
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva met with the Emir of Qatar. During the meeting, they discussed expanding mutual relations and advancing new joint initiatives. Further details are available at the provided link.

item.title: Flights from Bishkek to Moscow and Novosibirsk delayed
item.description: Flights by Russian airlines Aeroflot and S7 Airlines from Bishkek to Moscow and Novosibirsk were delayed on September 3. Kyrgyzstan Airports, a state enterprise, reported the delays without explaining the reasons.

item.title: Uzbekistan is a driving force in the Organization of Turkic States, says Secretary General
item.description: Kubanychbek Omuraliev, Secretary General of the Organization of Turkic States, congratulated Uzbekistan on its 35th Independence Day. He highlighted Uzbekistan's significant contributions to the Turkic world's unity through initiatives in transport, trade, digital transformation, education, culture, and regional dialogue. Omuraliev noted Uzbekistan's reforms under President Shavkat Mirziyoyev have strengthened its international standing.

item.title: UN Women's Fund Needs $150 Million to Combat Violence Against Women
item.description: The UN Trust Fund to End Violence Against Women has mobilized over $250 million and supported over 700 initiatives globally in 30 years. Despite successes, the situation remains dire, with 90% of women's organizations facing financial losses and nearly half at risk of closure.

item.title: Road collapses in Tashkent, one person injured
item.description: A section of road in Tashkent collapsed while cars were moving, injuring one person. Veolia Energy, Tashkent City Water Supply JSC, and Hududgaz Poytaxt gas supply branch commented on reports that an underground pipe caused the incident.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Critics of authorities continue to face persecution, hopes for thaw fade
item.description: The International Partnership for Human Rights (IPHR) report indicates that critics of the authorities in Kyrgyzstan continue to face persecution. Despite the dismissal of Kamchybek Tashiev from the State Committee for National Security, hopes for a thaw in the situation are diminishing.

item.title: Uzbekistan's service exports, driven by tourism, become largest income source
item.description: Uzbekistan's foreign trade turnover reached $49.5 billion in Jan-Jul, an 8.1% increase. Exports fell 3.6% to $19.93 billion, while imports rose 17.8% to $29.6 billion. Service exports, boosted by tourism, have become the largest source of income, despite a 63.1% drop in gold exports.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Secures Second Kok-Boru Victory at World Nomad Games
item.description: The Kyrgyzstan national team achieved its second consecutive victory in the kok-boru tournament at the 6th World Nomad Games, defeating Uzbekistan 16-11. Kyrgyzstan currently leads its group with six points.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev congratulates Mirziyoyev on Uzbekistan's 35th Independence Day at SCO Summit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev congratulated Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov on their countries' 35th independence anniversaries during the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan. Tokayev thanked Kyrgyzstan for its hospitality and praised the SCO's growth into a major international organization over 25 years, emphasizing mutual trust and respect for sovereignty.

item.title: Road collapses on Glinka Street in Tashkent, one injured
item.description: A section of asphalt collapsed on Glinka Street in Tashkent's Yakkasaroy district, creating a crack. Social media suggests an underground pipe explosion caused the incident. Several cars were damaged, and one person sustained minor injuries, receiving prompt medical attention. Traffic on Glinka Street is temporarily suspended.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Security Council emphasizes maintaining high security for World Nomad Games
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Security Council Secretary Adilet Orozbekov stated that major international events held recently concluded without incident, crediting joint efforts of security forces. He stressed the need to maintain heightened security measures throughout the VI World Nomad Games in Cholpon-Ata. Additional instructions were given to state bodies and local authorities.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Significantly Increased Fines for Aviation Violations
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Civil Aviation Agency is proposing substantial increases to fines for aviation-related offenses. The draft legislation, now open for public discussion, could see penalties rise severalfold, with some fines increasing by over 30 times. For instance, fines for airspace violations could jump from 7,500 to 100,000 som for individuals and from 23,000 to 500,000 som for legal entities.

item.title: Climate Change to Disproportionately Affect Vulnerable Groups in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Climate change in Kyrgyzstan is predicted to most severely impact vulnerable populations, including women, children, the elderly, people with disabilities, and low-income families. The National Adaptation Plan highlights that over 57% of the population relies on agriculture, making them susceptible to droughts and water shortages. Women, often responsible for household water and food, face increased burdens as resources decline.

item.title: Four Uzbek citizens arrested in South Korea for financing terrorism
item.description: Four Uzbek citizens have been arrested in South Korea on suspicion of financing a terrorist group in Syria. One individual allegedly sent $4,600 in cryptocurrency to the "Katiba at-Tavhid val-Jihod" terrorist organization. He is also suspected of purchasing vehicles and excavators for the group.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank tightens rules for anonymous cash deposits
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan is proposing changes to tighten rules for anonymous cash deposits into bank accounts, cards, and e-wallets via payment terminals. The new regulations would require user identification for such transactions, excluding low-risk payments like utilities and taxes.

item.title: Eurasian Economic Union Launches Traceability Mechanism for Foreign Goods
item.description: Starting September 1, 2026, the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) implemented a traceability mechanism for foreign goods cleared in one member state and moved to others. Initially, it covers refrigerators, washing machines, and televisions. The system aims to protect businesses from unfair competition and assure consumers of legal import.

item.title: Bishkek City Court Hears "Letters 75" Case, Continues Interrogating Defendants
item.description: The Bishkek City Court has concluded witness interrogations in the "Letters 75" case and begun questioning the accused. The case involves individuals who signed an appeal for early presidential elections. Previously, defendants were found guilty of violent power seizure and received suspended sentences and property confiscation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Expand Meat Imports from India and Grow Jute on 50,000 Hectares
item.description: Uzbekistan and India intend to expand cooperation in agriculture and food. Uzbekistan is interested in increasing meat imports from India and is testing new salt-tolerant cotton varieties. Joint ventures are being established for meat production, with significant plans for the coming years.

item.title: Tajikistan faces mudslide threat in mountain regions September 3-4
item.description: Tajikistan's Agency for Hydrometeorology warns of mudslides in mountainous areas of republican subordination, Sughd region, and western Gorno-Badakhshan from September 3-4. Authorities advise residents to avoid livestock grazing, wood gathering, fishing, and hunting, and tour companies to cancel mountain hikes.

item.title: Uzbekistan President holds dialogue on improving business conditions
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with entrepreneurs in Khiva to discuss improving conditions for businesses. The focus shifted from supporting startups to fostering growth for existing enterprises, emphasizing access to finance, technology, markets, and a predictable regulatory environment. Business credit portfolios have nearly tripled.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Organize Free Extracurricular Classes for Children from Poor Families
item.description: Uzbekistan will establish free extracurricular clubs in schools, technical schools, and educational centers for children from low-income families. This initiative aims to address the lack of specific programs for engaging impoverished youth in vocational training. Youth leaders, district governor's assistants, and women's activists will be tasked with organizing these clubs.

item.title: Two Individuals Apprehended Attempting to Smuggle $240,000 Out of Uzbekistan
item.description: Customs officials at the "Navoi" border post in Tashkent region intercepted two individuals attempting to smuggle $240,000 out of Uzbekistan. One woman was found with $80,000 and the other with $160,000, concealed and strapped to their legs under clothing. The State Customs Committee reported the incident and released video footage.

item.title: Crimean Tatar Athletes Representing Ukraine Received Applause in Bishkek
item.description: Refat Chubarov, head of the Crimean Tatar National Assembly, stated that Crimean Tatar athletes representing Ukraine at the opening ceremony of the VI World Nomad Games in Bishkek were met with applause. He noted that the Ukrainian delegation, though small, received enthusiastic reception. Leaders from various countries attended the event.
